_doc: Everything about these two papers that the page shows as data. mk_paper.py turns it into the headline card, Further reading and window.PAPER. This page covers two papers, so 'papers' lists both; A is Encoder-Decoder Gemma, B is T5Gemma 2.
title: Encoder-Decoder Gemma and T5Gemma 2

papers.title: Encoder-Decoder Gemma: Improving the Quality-Efficiency Trade-Off via Adaptation
papers.authors: Biao Zhang, Fedor Moiseev, Joshua Ainslie, Paul Suganthan, Min Ma, Surya Bhupatiraju, Fede Lebron, Orhan Firat, Armand Joulin, Zhe Dong
papers.note: the method paper, called T5Gemma when the weights were released. Read Sections 3, 5 and 6; the discussion section is where the ablations that matter live (bidirectional attention, cross-attention warmup, adaptation against from scratch).

papers.title: T5Gemma 2: Seeing, Reading, and Understanding Longer
papers.authors: Biao Zhang, Paul Suganthan, Gaël Liu, Ilya Philippov, Sahil Dua, Ben Hora, Kat Black, Gus Martins, Omar Sanseviero, Shreya Pathak, Cassidy Hardin, Francesco Visin, Jiageng Zhang, Kathleen Kenealy, Qin Yin, Xiaodan Song, Olivier Lacombe, Armand Joulin, Tris Warkentin, Adam Roberts
papers.note: shorter, and the one to read if you care about long context or multimodality. Tables 4 and 5 are the whole argument.

authors_short: Biao Zhang, Fedor Moiseev, Joshua Ainslie, Paul Suganthan, Min Ma, Surya Bhupatiraju, Fede Lebron, Orhan Firat, Armand Joulin, Zhe Dong (Google); for T5Gemma 2, Biao Zhang, Paul Suganthan, Gaël Liu, Ilya Philippov et al. (Google DeepMind, 20 authors)
takeaway: Adapts pretrained decoder-only checkpoints into encoder-decoder models by copying weights across and continuing with UL2 or PrefixLM, which is cheaper than pretraining from scratch and also better above roughly 100M params; gains land after instruction tuning (9B-9B over Gemma 2 9B by 4.9, 2B-2B by 7.1), encoder-decoder wins SuperGLUE at every scale, and the asymmetric 9B-2B matches Gemma 2 2B's latency at far higher quality. T5Gemma 2 carries the recipe to Gemma 3 with tied embeddings and merged attention, and its long-context result is the strongest in the line: 81.7 on RULER 32K at 4B-4B against Gemma 3 4B's 66.8, despite pretraining at only 16K.
verdict: Believe the recipe and its direction: copied decoder weights plus a bidirectional encoder match the source model after pretraining and beat it after tuning, at matched inference cost. Treat the size of the wins as single runs from models with about twice the parameters, and the long-context lead as real at 32K but narrowing by 128K.

kb.n: 2019: the original encoder-decoder against decoder-only result being retested, the span corruption that UL2 extends, and the tied embeddings T5Gemma 2 returns to. Its page animates the three attention masks.
2025: the compute-matched encoder against decoder comparison from the representation-learning side; T5Gemma is the same question from the generation side.
2024: the other route to bidirectional prompt processing, a bidirectional pass inside a decoder-only model instead of splitting the model in two.

kb.t: End-to-End Context Compression at Scale (Latent Context Language Models)
kb.n: 2026: the complementary answer for long inputs, compressing the context into latents for a decoder rather than restructuring the model around an encoder.
2020: the reason the field went the other way (few-shot prompting of one decoder stack), and the capability neither T5Gemma paper tests.
2017: the encoder-decoder this adapts back to, run live at toy scale on its page.
2018: the bidirectional encoder on its own; SuperGLUE as the test of representations.
